title: Suspected carjacker dies 'in custody'
article: A 25-year-old man allegedly punched and kicked by Edmonton police officers during his arresthas died.
Mark Milakovic died in hospital Thursday morning. He faced several charges in connection with a carjacking on Saturday.
"This is being treated as an in-custody death and the incident is still under investigation,"says anews release from Edmonton police.
A spokesperson for the medical examiner's office said Thursday that an autopsyfound no injuries that caused or contributed to his death.
The final cause of death won't be known until toxicology results come back, in about six to eight weeks.
Officers had said theysaw the man swallow what was believed to be cocaine before his arrestSaturday.
Chief Mike Boyd told reporters on Sunday that he had called in the Calgary force to review the arrest after some witnesses made the allegations about the officers during media interviews.
At the time, Boyd said he wanted to "allay the concerns of the public based on inferences presented in the media about the circumstances of the arrest."
The incident began at around 11 a.m. MT on Saturday.
A man hijacked a car at a stoplightat 137 Avenue and 127 Street in the city's west end, then drove off. Police chased the car into the city's centre, where it got stuck in traffic.
Officers boxed the vehicle in at 102 Street and MacDonald Drive. They pulled the suspect out, but in the struggle he suffered what police are calling a "medical episode."
An officer administered CPR and the man was later revived in an ambulance.
Milakovic faced several charges, including robbery and possession of drugs for the purpose of trafficking.
Solicitor General Harvey Cenaiko announced Tuesday that Alberta is forminga team of investigators that would look intoallegations of criminal activity bypolice officers.
The new unit would be made up of veteran officers from existing forces, but wouldn't include civilians, he said. He hopes to have more details by the fall.
